## 📚 Overview

This is an **API Testing Automation** project built using a **BDD (Behavior Driven Development)** approach with Cucumber, HTML reports for test result visualization, and Faker for data generation.

### ✨ Features

- ✅ **BDD Framework**: Cucumber with Gherkin syntax
- ✅ **HTML Reporting**: Portable test reports with execution summaries
- ✅ **HTML Report**: Simple HTML reporting format
- ✅ **Auto Generate Data**: Using @faker-js/faker for random data
- ✅ **Modular Structure**: Separate test files per request type
- ✅ **Multi Scenarios**: Minimum 2 scenarios per endpoint for comprehensive coverage
- ✅ **Automated Reports**: Reports are generated after successful test runs
- ✅ **CI/CD Ready**: GitHub Actions integration included
- ✅ **JSON Reports**: Cucumber JSON output for further processing

## 📋 Prerequisites

Before running this project, ensure you have:

- Node.js 22.x or 24.x installed
- npm or yarn package manager

## 🚀 Installation

### 1. Clone the Repository
```bash
git clone https://github.com/yourusername/api-test-automation.git
cd api-test-automation
```

### 2. Install Dependencies
```bash
npm install
```

### 3. Configure Environment
Create `.env` file in root directory:
```env
API_BASE_URL=https://reqres.in/api
TEST_ENV=production
GITHUB_TOKEN=""  # Optional: For API authentication if needed
```

---

## 🎮 Running Tests

### Run All Tests (Recommended)
```bash
npm run test
```
This command runs all tests and generates reports automatically.

### Run Specific Request Tests

#### GET Users Tests
```bash
npx @cucumber/cucumber tests/features/get_users.feature --require tests/support/index.ts --format progress
```

#### Single User Tests
```bash
npx @cucumber/cucumber tests/features/get_single_user.feature --require tests/support/index.ts --format progress
```

#### POST Users Tests
```bash
npx @cucumber/cucumber tests/features/post_users.feature --require tests/support/index.ts --format progress
```

#### PUT Users Tests
```bash
npx @cucumber/cucumber tests/features/put_users.feature --require tests/support/index.ts --format progress
```

#### DELETE Users Tests
```bash
npx @cucumber/cucumber tests/features/delete_users.feature --require tests/support/index.ts --format progress
```

### Run Single Scenario
```bash
npx @cucumber/cucumber tests/features/get_users.feature --name "Verify GET users list response structure" --require tests/support/index.ts --format progress
```

### Run Tests with Verbose Output
```bash
npx @cucumber/cucumber tests/features/**/*.feature --require tests/support/index.ts --format progress
```

## 🎭 Feature Files Overview

Each feature file represents one request type with at least 2 scenarios:

### 1. GET /users (`get_users.feature`)
- Verify GET users list response structure
- Validate users list contains valid user data

### 2. GET /users/:id (`get_single_user.feature`)
- Verify get valid user by ID
- Verify get non-existent user returns error

### 3. POST /users (`post_users.feature`)
- Create user with valid random data (generated by Faker)
- Verify user creation contains required fields

### 4. PUT /users/:id (`put_users.feature`)
- Update user with valid patch data
- Verify user update contains timestamp

### 5. DELETE /users/:id (`delete_users.feature`)
- Delete user with valid ID
- Delete non-existent user returns appropriate response

---

## 🔬 Example Test Scenario

```gherkin
Feature: Create New User
    As a test engineer
    I want to test user creation functionality
    So that I can verify new users can be created via API

    Scenario: Create user with valid random data
        Given I have a valid create user endpoint
        When I add a user with random data
        And I make a POST request to create user
        Then the response status should be created successfully
        And the created user should contain "id"
```

## 🔄 CI/CD Pipeline with GitHub Actions

This project includes GitHub Actions workflows for automated testing:

### Workflow 1: CI Pipeline (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`)
- Runs on every push to main branch
- Runs on every Pull Request
- Installs dependencies
- Executes all test suites
- Generates reports
- Uploads test artifacts

### Workflow 2: Nightly Tests (`.github/workflows/nightly.yml`)
- Scheduled to run daily at 2 AM UTC
- Useful for long-running integration tests
- Automatically notifies team of failures

### View Pipeline Results
Navigate to the **Actions** tab in your GitHub repository after pushing changes.

## 🏗️ CI/CD Setup

### For Your Own GitHub Repository

1. Create a new repository on GitHub
2. Push your code:
   ```bash
   git init
   git add .
   git commit -m "Initial commit: AI-generated API test suite"
   git branch -M main
   git remote add origin https://github.com/yourusername/api-test-automation.git
   git push -u origin main
   ```

3. GitHub Actions will automatically pick up the workflow files from `.github/workflows/`

4. Configure Secrets (if needed):
   ```bash
   # Go to your repository settings > Secrets and variables > Actions
   # Add any sensitive tokens or keys here
   ```

### Customizing Workflows

Edit the workflow YAML files in `.github/workflows/` to customize:
- Trigger conditions
- Node.js versions
- Test configurations
- Notification settings

## ⚠️ Known Limitations

- **Rate Limiting**: External API (reqres.in) has strict rate limits
  - Solution: Use mock servers for production testing
  - Recommended: Mockoon, MSW, or Postman Mock Server
  
- **POST/PUT Success Rate**: May experience 429 errors due to API limits
  - These failures are expected behavior from external provider
